mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -38.9 to -35.7 over the last four weeks, a roughly 3.2-point gain reflecting sustained recovery momentum; this autocorrelated trend is expected to continue, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days versus the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -38.9 to -35.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the recent uptrend did not persist.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility plateaued near -22 for three straight weeks after an earlier sharp recovery from -27.1, indicating essential-trip demand has saturated; without further gains in baseline necessity travel, discretionary RETAIL_REC growth will stall or reverse over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change stays below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved -22.1,-22.3,-22.4 across last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days rises above the prior 14-day mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, rejecting the saturation linkage.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have moved together in a narrow stable band (-39 to -38 and -31 to -30 respectively) for four weeks, indicating a stable commuting floor; any joint uptick in both series together would raise incidental weekday retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next month, whereas continued joint stagnation keeps RETAIL_REC flat.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stable within a few points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by more than 3 points jointly over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite both remaining flat.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has remained low and stable (6-7 percent above baseline) for four weeks, indicating no new stay-at-home policy pressure; in this no-restriction regime, retail recovery is expected to continue its gradual upward path over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 6.0 and 7.4 across four weeks
regime_hint: no new restriction, endemic policy regime
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL spikes above 10 (signaling new restrictions) while RETAIL_REC still rises, or RESIDENTIAL stays flat but RETAIL_REC declines, either of which breaks the policy-linked mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has surged from 3.0 to 14.4 over four weeks, consistent with peak summer outdoor recreation; this seasonal substitution draws discretionary trips away from indoor retail and recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 3.0 to 14.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 7 days rises in tandem with continued PARKS growth, rejecting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues to climb above 15 percent and holds there for a week, sustained outdoor-recreation substitution will further suppress retail footfall, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 15 points for one full week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 14.4 at t-0w, near the 15-point threshold
failure_condition: PARKS crosses above 15 but RETAIL_REC mean over the following two weeks does not decline relative to the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stagnated near -30 to -31 for four weeks despite other series showing modest change, indicating suppressed public transit use that limits the commuting- and errand-linked foot traffic feeding retail locations; this persistent suppression will keep RETAIL_REC from rising over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT held between -31.6 and -30.0 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days increases even though TRANSIT remains within the same -30 to -32 band, rejecting the transit-suppression linkage.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of flat-to-declining WORKPLACES (-39.0 to -39.6) combined with flat RESIDENTIAL (6-7) suggests an entrenched hybrid-work equilibrium rather than active policy change; this dual stability removes any upward pressure from return-to-office commuting, so RETAIL_REC will remain roughly flat rather than rising over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined slightly from -39.0 to -39.6 while RESIDENTIAL held 6.0-7.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 points over the next 28 days despite both WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL remaining within their current narrow bands, rejecting the joint-stability dampening mechanism.
